tasks.short: Recover dust impressions for fingerprint examination

steps.what: Collect dust impressions from surfaces while preserving location, condition and evidence identity
Examine recovered impressions for fingerprint information and record identification limitations

tasks.design: Retain impression recovery and examination with the technician, keeping observations in {DOCS}. Existing reference and imaging aids can support examination, but they do not replace physical recovery or establish identity on their own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Surface conditions and fragile traces require situational recovery choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing collection and reference tools support the task without removing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recovery can damage weak traces, and partial impressions may not support an identification.
tasks.human_edge: The technician preserves evidence and recognises limits in what it can support.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in physical recovery or examination workload.

reach.learn: Communicate recovery conditions and uncertainty without overstating identification.

evidence.claim: Physical impression recovery and examination remain human work, based on model knowledge; no digest fingerprint automation capability applies.

assumptions: Boundary is recovery and initial examination, excluding specialist comparisons and external testimony.
Technician produces impression identity, location and condition during s1 and examination observations in s2; no free structured suitability or identification flag is assumed.
Consider native imaging and record tools first. Zero upkeep because no new automation or capture workflow is proposed.
unknowns: Recovery methods and existing imaging aids
research_questions: Which surface conditions require a different recovery method or specialist examination?

already_counted.description: All recovery, preservation and examination remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Physical evidence recovery and initial interpretation are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine crime scene blood stain patterns

steps.what: Examine blood stain patterns, scene geometry and contextual evidence while recording observations and limitations

tasks.design: Keep scene examination and blood stain interpretation with the technician, recording evidence and alternatives in {DOCS}. Existing measurement tools assist observation; no automated reconstruction or causal conclusion is established here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patterns depend on surfaces, intervening events and incomplete scene information.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documentation tools support scrutiny without replacing examination.
tasks.still_hard: Several mechanisms may explain similar observed patterns.
tasks.human_edge: The technician separates observation from interpretation and records competing explanations.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in scene examination or interpretive effort.

reach.learn: Communicate alternative explanations and avoid inferring unsupported event details.

evidence.claim: Retaining scene-specific blood stain examination is model knowledge; the digest provides no validated reconstruction capability.

assumptions: Boundary is pattern examination and technical assessment; evidence collection by other specialists and external case conclusions are separate.
Technician produces observations and qualified interpretations in s1; no structured stain type or causal reconstruction is assumed beforehand.
Consider existing native measurement tools first. Zero upkeep because no new tool or record process is introduced.
research_questions: What independent scene evidence could distinguish the leading competing interpretations?

already_counted.description: All scene observation and qualified interpretation remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. No scene examination or interpretive work is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse gunshot residue and bullet paths

steps.what: Analyze gunshot residue and bullet paths against physical evidence and alternative shooting explanations

tasks.design: Retain residue and path interpretation with the technician using {DOCS} for evidence and qualifications. Existing analytical and measurement tools support particular observations, while combining them into an event explanation remains human analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transfer, contamination and uncertain geometry complicate causal interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing analytical records support examination without establishing autonomous reconstruction.
tasks.still_hard: Residue or a possible path alone may not establish who fired or the complete event sequence.
tasks.human_edge: The technician tests alternative explanations and avoids stronger conclusions than the evidence supports.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in forensic analysis or change in conclusion authority.

reach.learn: State geometric uncertainty and distinguish compatible paths from proven events.

evidence.claim: Combining residue and trajectory evidence requires case-specific judgement, based on model knowledge; no applicable digest automation case is present.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician analysis, excluding specialist laboratory execution and formal testimony.
Technician checks measurements and records uncertainties during s1; no preclassified shooting sequence or residue significance is assumed.
Consider existing native measurement and analysis tools first. Zero upkeep because no new automation is introduced.
research_questions: Which proposed event details remain unsupported after accounting for transfer and geometric uncertainty?

already_counted.description: All evidence analysis and qualification remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. The proposal removes no physical evidence interpretation or hypothesis testing.

steps.what: Confer with experts about evidence, conflicting interpretations and specialist examination needs

tasks.design: Retain evidence discussions with specialists through {TELEPHONY}. Existing case records support the conversation, while resolving uncertainty and defining specialist questions requires direct scientific exchange.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different disciplines bring evidence limits that cannot be resolved through routine routing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared records support discussion without replacing expert interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Apparent agreement can hide differing assumptions about the evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The technician asks clarifying questions and surfaces contradictions between specialist views.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in specialist discussion time.

reach.learn: Frame precise questions and preserve discipline-specific uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Specialist forensic consultation remains human work, based on model knowledge; no preparation saving is assumed without an observed preparation step.

assumptions: Boundary is the focal technician's consultation time; specialist labour is outside the denominator and unchanged.
Specialists supply their observations during the live discussion; no consensus or interpretive classification is assumed as a structured input.
Consider native case-record access first. Zero upkeep because no new capture, transcription or automation is introduced.
research_questions: Which interpretive disagreements require new examination rather than further discussion?

already_counted.description: All focal consultation and question clarification remain counted.

incremental.description: No additional upkeep or specialist transfer introduced.
